result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_dominating_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a set of nodes forms a dominating set. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22777-L22852){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_dominating_set(nodes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A dominating set `D` of a graph `G = (V, E)` is a subset of V such that every vertex not in `D` is adjacent to at least one member of `D`. In other words, every node is either in `D` or has a neighbor in `D`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs to check. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the nodes form a valid dominating set, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} A dominating set covers every vertex either directly or via a neighbor, so validation is a single pass: mark every element of the input set plus every one of their neighbors, then verify that every vertex in the graph is now marked. The scan costs $O(V + E)$. Edge cases behave predictably: the empty set dominates only the empty graph, and the entire vertex set is always a dominating set (trivially). A single-node set dominates exactly that node and its neighborhood. ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path `A-B-C-D`, the set `{B, D}` dominates the whole graph: `B` covers `A` and `C`, while `D` covers itself: ::: {#0b6e3d38 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) b_id = graph.get_id_from_label("B") d_id = graph.get_id_from_label("D") # Returns True graph.is_dominating_set([b_id, d_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Dropping `D` leaves it uncovered, since `B` alone doesn't reach that far: ::: {#fd8bf83d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False: D is neither in the set nor adjacent to a member graph.is_dominating_set([b_id]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: ::: This is a convenient way to confirm a dominating set produced by `dominating_set()` is actually valid: ::: {#0727b470 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_gnm_graph(n=50, m=100, seed=23) dom = graph.dominating_set() # Returns True: dominating_set() always produces a valid result graph.is_dominating_set(dom) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
